The bill would let aged care providers keep getting government subsidies during declared emergencies, such as pandemics or natural disasters.
It would stop providers from charging residents a fee to hold their place in a facility during an emergency.

The Aged Care Legislation Amendment (Emergency Leave) Bill 2020 introduces a new emergency leave type for permanent aged-care residents during pandemics, natural disasters, or other large-scale emergencies, allowing them to take leave without financial burden or losing their room, with retrospective application from 1 April 2020.

The Aged Care Legislation Amendment (Emergency Leave) Bill 2020 creates emergency leave for permanent residential aged-care residents during emergencies, removing the 52-day social leave cap and the $230 daily cost to families, backdated to 1 April 2020.
